children: is down ~31% in Monday morning trading after reporting topline results from a phase 2 trial of CUE-221 for chronic spontaneous urticaria.
Data from the study, conducted in China, found that CUE-221 led to a higher percentage of complete resolution of hives—the primary endpoint—compared to Genentech
Xolair (omalizumab) in all three doses examined.

The response was dose dependent as the 4 mg/kg dose, the highest tested, achieved the greatest resolution percentage, 54%, compared to Xolair, 41%, at week 12. The two lower doses, 2 mg/kg and 1 mg/kg, led to resolutions of, respectively, 53% and 43%,
A secondary endpoint, complete response, was only met with statistical significance at the 4 mg/kg dose.
Cue said that based on the data, it is planning a "rapid initiation of a phase 2b/3 study" in the indication.

Despite the positive results, the stock could be down so negatively as the data was sourced from China, which has drawn skepticism from many in other trials. Investors may have also wanted to see a bigger difference in hive resolution between CUE-221 and Xolair.

title: Cue Biopharma plummets on phase 2 data for chronic spontaneous urticaria asset
